extracted.intended_audience: senior undergraduate and first‑year graduate students applying for the DOE Computational Science Graduate Fellowship (U.S. citizens and lawful permanent residents)
extracted.subtask_description: Information and program requirements for applicants to the Department of Energy Computational Science Graduate Fellowship (CSGF), describing who is eligible, the benefits offered, and expectations such as the DOE laboratory practicum and community participation. Targets students pursuing doctoral degrees using high‑performance computing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fields of study / program purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department of Energy Computational Science Graduate Fellowship (DOE CSGF) provides outstanding opportunities to students pursuing doctoral degrees in fields that use high-performance computing to solve complex science and engineering problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program fosters a community of Ph.D. students, alumni, DOE laboratory staff and scientists who want to have an impact on the nation while advancing their research. (This phrasing indicates that eligible/competitive applicants should be pursuing Ph.D. work that relies on HPC to address significant science or engineering problems.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Citizenship / residency eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Open to U.S. citizens and lawful permanent residents

rubrics_metrics.name: Target applicant stage
rubrics_metrics.description: Seeks senior undergrads and first-year graduate students
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program targets students at or just before the transition to full-time doctoral study (i.e., seniors and first‑year grad students preparing to pursue a Ph.D.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Enrollment / recipient status requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must be full-time doctoral students
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awardees are expected to be enrolled as full‑time Ph.D. students (this is a condition for receiving/support continuation of the fellowship).

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial benefits and renewal
rubrics_metrics.description: $45,000 annual stipend; payment of full tuition and fees; Yearly professional development allowance; Renewable up to four years
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes the fellowship's funding package and that support may be renewed for multiple years (up to four), which implies expectations for continued satisfactory progress/enrollment for renewal.

rubrics_metrics.name: DOE Laboratory Practicum — duration and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: The practicum is a unique opportunity for DOE CSGF fellows to work in a DOE laboratory ... The practicum takes place over a 12-week-minimum period, typically in the summer months, where fellows relocate to the facility and contribute to the work of the laboratory's multidisciplinary teams – most often with ties to high-performance computing resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellows work outside of their thesis studies, use the practicum to learn new skills and expand research capabilities, relocate to the host facility, and contribute to multidisciplinary teams. The page frames the practicum as an expected component of the fellowship experience and valuable professional development (including a fellow quote about confidence-building and starting new projects).

rubrics_metrics.name: Program participation and professional opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaborations with fellows, lab staff and beyond; Annual meeting to share research and strengthen connections; Outreach via DEIXIS magazine/online and the 'Science in Parallel' podcast.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fellowship emphasizes community engagement, networking, collaborations, and dissemination opportunities (annual meeting, publications, podcast). Competitive/typical fellows are expected to take part in these community and professional-development activities; alumni outcomes include careers in industry, academia and national laboratories.
